# Stelline

> Stelline is a calm Star Battle-style logic puzzle game for iPhone (iOS 26 or later) and Android (Android 9 or later). Every board is generated on the device and verified to have exactly one solution, then graded Easy to Expert by the same seventeen-technique deduction engine that powers its hints. Paid once (USD 1.99 on both stores), no ads, no account, no data collected. Version 1.1 adds Today's board, the same board for everyone for one UTC day, with optional Game Center leaderboards (iPhone only for now) and shareable board links.

Stelline (Italian for "little stars") is made by Andelis Studio, an independent one-person studio, and written from scratch in Swift, including its own generator, solver and deduction engine, which run on both platforms; the Android interface is native Kotlin and Jetpack Compose. This file follows the llms.txt convention and summarises the site at https://stelline.page for answer engines and assistants. Last updated 17 October 2026.

## Docs

- [Support and FAQ](https://stelline.page/support/): question-and-answer page covering the rules, modes and board sizes, controls, hints, difficulty levels, Today's board and leaderboards, accessibility, requirements, privacy and how to report a problem.
- [Privacy policy](https://stelline.page/privacy/): what the app collects (nothing), what the optional Game Center leaderboards send to Apple on iPhone, what the Android app does (no permissions, no data), and what this website does (no cookies, no analytics).
- [Press kit](https://stelline.page/press/): app icon, screenshots, 50/100/300-word descriptions, fact sheet (price, sizes, iOS and Android versions, no ads, no data) and the press contact.
- [Solving techniques](https://stelline.page/techniques/): the fourteen Star Battle techniques of the hint ladder and the lessons, each explained on a real board drawn on the page (last cells, nosy neighbours, line lock, two-by-two blocks, exclusion, clumps, container consumption, counting rows and regions, X-wing, finned count, squeeze, set difference, fish, the what-if step), the two habits before them (dots around a placed piece, finished units) and the sheet of common two-star shapes.
- [Home page](https://stelline.page/): overview and screenshots.

## App

- [Stelline on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6808032290): free to download since version 1.5 (Today's boards, Daily Rush, Learn, a Starter set of boards and two new boards a day are free); Stelline Unlimited (USD 1.99, one-time, Family Sharing) opens the generator without limit, and stats and history; no ads, no subscription.
- [Stelline on Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=studio.andelis.stelline): USD 1.99, paid once with everything in it, no in-app purchases, no ads.
- Platform: iPhone and iPad (iOS and iPadOS 26 or later; the iPad app also runs on Apple-silicon Macs) and Android phones and tablets (Android 9 or later, 64-bit); not Apple Watch. Portrait on phones; tablets rotate, with the board at full height beside the controls in landscape and a 12×12 one-queen size. Languages: English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Japanese and Brazilian Portuguese (the app follows the phone's language; on Android 13 or later a per-app language can be chosen in the system settings; the website and support are in English). Category: Games, Puzzle. Age rating 4+ on the App Store.
- Board links: https://stelline.page/b/<code> opens a shared board in Stelline when the app is installed, on iPhone or on Android (Android App Links); otherwise the page shows the board's id, size, mode and region map with a link to the App Store.

- [Contact form](https://tally.so/r/Pdx98x): hosted by Tally, no account needed; only what you type is sent.
- [Ideas board](https://stelline.featurebase.app/): public roadmap and feature requests; vote or post as a guest.

## Facts

- Stelline is a Star Battle-style logic puzzle: place queens (or stars) so that every row, every column and every colour region holds exactly the required number, and no two pieces touch, not even diagonally.
- Two modes: 1 queen (one queen per row, column and region) on 6×6 to 11×11 boards, and 2 stars (two stars per row, column and region) on 9×9 to 11×11 boards. Compete (version 1.2) holds Today's board in both modes, a numbered archive of every past daily board (#1 is 12 September 2026, one number per day in each mode) and Enter a code; on these boards Auto-check, auto-dots and hints are off for everyone, whatever the settings, so every time is made on equal terms. Past boards can be played any day; their times stay on the phone and are not posted.
- Every board has exactly one solution. Boards are generated on the phone, so there is no pack to run out of and nothing to download, and an exact solver checks each one before it is shown.
- Four difficulty tiers, Easy, Medium, Hard and Expert, graded by a deduction engine with seventeen techniques that solves each board the way a person would. The grade does not depend on the board size. Easy, Medium and Hard boards need direct deductions only in both modes (2 stars has no Easy); Expert boards need what-if reasoning, one level in 1 queen mode; a few Expert 2 stars boards need more than the hints can explain.
- Hints are unlimited, with no cooldown, and work in stages: two counters (misplaced queens, misplaced dots) that never say where; then "Show me where", which highlights the row, column or region behind the next logical step, then the exact cells, names the technique and applies it on request; a mistake on the board is narrowed down to the region, then the cells, and cleared on request. "Reveal" places one solution piece only when no logical step exists. A solve with no hints and no conflicts earns the Flawless badge.
- Controls: tap a cell to cycle empty, dot, queen or star; drag across cells to dot them (start on a dot to erase). A placed piece dots its eight neighbours automatically; completed rows, columns and regions can dot themselves too. Auto-check stripes pieces that touch or exceed a row, column or region. Undo, redo and clear, with the history saved alongside the game. A timer that can be hidden. No lives, no streaks.
- The game saves itself after every move; the Home screen shows Continue with the board size and time so far.
- Fully offline: no internet connection is needed, ever, and nothing is downloaded after installation.
- No data collected: no account, no ads, no analytics, no third-party code and no network code beyond the optional Game Center leaderboards. The App Store privacy label is "Data Not Collected" and the Google Play Data safety section says no data is collected or shared. Settings and saved games stay on the phone and are deleted with the app.
- Appearance: an original pastel palette with a named colour for every region, a Classic black-and-white theme with heavy region borders, a Colour-blind mode with high-contrast colours and thicker borders, and light, dark or system appearance. Crown or star pieces, dot or X marks.
- Accessibility: on iPhone, full VoiceOver support (every cell announces its state, region colour, row and column, with actions to mark, place and clear), Dynamic Type, Reduce Motion, and haptics that can be turned off. On Android, TalkBack reads every cell (piece, region colour, row, column), and the font size and remove-animations settings are respected.
- Today's board (version 1.1): the same board for every player for 24 hours, a 9×9 board in 1 queen mode and a 10×10 board in 2 stars mode, generated on the phone from the UTC date, so no connection is needed. The same engine runs on iPhone and Android, so Today's board is the same board on both on any given day. The day changes at midnight UTC. Marks, undo history and time are kept per day and mode.
- Game Center leaderboards (version 1.1, iPhone only for now): optional and off by default. When turned on in Settings, the app posts the time on Today's board to the day's leaderboard for that mode (lower is better, reset daily). Everything else works without it, entirely offline.
- Board links (version 1.1): every board has an id and a shareable link of the form https://stelline.page/b/<code>; a friend opens it with one tap when Stelline is installed, or types the code under Compete.
- Version 1.1 also brings a redesigned Home screen and asks for confirmation before Clear or New puzzle wipes a game in progress.
- Tactics (version 1.4, iPhone): a three-minute rush of positions to read. Every position is a board part-way through a solve; the player taps the cell where a queen (or star) can be proven right now. A right tap scores and moves on; a wrong tap costs one of three lives and shows the answer with the idea behind it, named and explained. Positions are cut from freshly generated boards by the same deduction engine as the hints; the best score stays on the phone.
- Learn (version 1.4 on iPhone, 1.0 on Android): lessons played on a real board, with the player making every move. First steps (rules and controls) opens by itself on a fresh install; a second lesson introduces 2-star mode; the six-slide rules summary is under Learn as The rules at a glance.
- Learn, Techniques and Advanced (version 1.6 on both platforms): one lesson per idea of the solver (last cells, nosy neighbours, line locks, two-by-two blocks, exclusion, clumps, container consumption, counting, X-wing, finned count; then squeezes, set differences, fish and the what-if step). Each lesson explains the idea on a real position, has the player make the deduction, shows a second position, then offers Practice this idea: fresh positions keyed on that idea, untimed, no lives, a counter of solved positions. The what-if lesson has no practice.
- What-if marks (version 1.6 on both platforms, off by default, Settings): a What if? button opens a branch; marks made in it are drawn hollow in the accent colour; Keep makes them firm, Drop removes them all in one step (undoable). One branch at a time.
- iPad (version 1.6): the board beside its controls in landscape, two columns on Home, keyboard and pointer support, Apple Pencil hover, 1-queen boards up to 12×12 on large screens; the iPad app runs on Apple-silicon Macs. On the Mac (verified for macOS on 16 October 2026; version 1.6.1 of 17 October adds a menu bar with shortcuts: New puzzle ⌘N, Undo ⌘Z, Hint ⌘/, What if? ⌘E, Home ⌘1 to Compete ⌘4, Settings ⌘,; right-click a cell for its marks; the same shortcuts on an iPad with a keyboard). Version 1.6.1 also adds Learn this on the hint banner and in the Tactics review, which opens the lesson behind the named idea, and the sheet of common two-star shapes under Learn. Android tablets and Chromebooks (version 1.6): the same two-pane landscape layout, keyboard and mouse.
- Android 1.6 (Google Play, published 15 October 2026): the version jumps from 1.0 to 1.6 and carries everything since: Tactics, Daily Rush, optional Play Games leaderboards (off until switched on), Stats, six pieces, the lessons, the what-if marks, tablets. The app still asks for no internet permission; the leaderboards go through Google Play services.
- Pieces (version 1.4, iPhone): besides the crown and the star, four drawn pieces, a donut, a cat, an elf and a teddy bear, the studio's own artwork; labels and hints still say queen or star.
- Android: Stelline for Android is on Google Play since 2 October 2026 (version 1.0) and at version 1.6 since 15 October 2026. Requirements: Android 9 or later, 64-bit phones and tablets, Chromebooks; portrait on phones, either way up on tablets. Same seven languages; the app follows the phone's language, and on Android 13 or later a per-app language can be chosen under Settings, Apps, Stelline, Language. Same price model: one purchase, no ads, no in-app purchases (USD 1.99). Same puzzle engine, so Today's board is the same board as on iPhone on any given day; board share links open the app on Android too when it is installed (Android App Links). Optional Play Games leaderboards since 1.6, off until switched on in Settings. The Android app requests no permissions at all, not even internet access (the leaderboards go through Google Play services); its Google Play Data safety section says no data is collected or shared. The only Google-run element is the Play Store itself (download, update, purchase, the optional in-app rating dialog shown by the Play Store app), processed by Google under Google's privacy policy. Android Auto Backup may include the app's saved data in the backups the user makes of the phone to their Google account, like any app; uninstalling deletes everything. Accessibility: TalkBack reads every cell (piece, region colour, row, column); font size and remove-animations settings are respected.
- Star Battle is a puzzle genre, created by Hans Eendebak for the 2003 World Puzzle Championship in the Netherlands. Apple, iPhone, App Store and Game Center are trademarks of Apple Inc. Google Play and Android are trademarks of Google LLC.
